title: Sitemaps
definition: An XML file (`sitemap.xml`) that acts as a roadmap of your website for search engines, listing all public URLs so Google doesn't have to guess where your pages are.
simpleExplanation: If your site has 5,000 blog posts, Google's bot might miss some if it just clicks around randomly. A sitemap is a list you hand directly to Google saying: 'Here are the exact 5,000 URLs I want you to rank in search results.'
realWorldExample: Creating a dynamic `sitemap.ts` file in Next.js that queries your database, gets all 5,000 blog post slugs, and automatically generates the XML file for Google.

basic: If you just have a 3-page portfolio site, do you strictly need a complex dynamic sitemap?
intermediate: How does Next.js automatically generate a sitemap using code?

answers.question: Strictly need it?
answers.answer: No. Google's crawlers are incredibly smart and will easily find 3 pages just by following the links in your Navbar. Sitemaps are critical for massive, dynamic sites with thousands of URLs.

answers.question: How to generate?
answers.answer: By creating a special `sitemap.ts` file at the root of the `app` directory that exports a default async function returning an array of URL objects.
